stories.delivered_paragraph: Amazon is requiring third-party sellers to label product images and videos containing AI-generated people, following a New York law that took effect last month. Sellers must add metadata tags to images and “A+” listing content, while the state’s first-in-the-nation rule requires disclosure when advertising uses photorealistic synthetic performers instead of human actors. The move could make Amazon a key test of how AI-ad disclosure laws are enforced at scale.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Eight Australian early-stage startups will pitch at Stripe Tour Sydney on August 19 in TechCrunch’s Startup Battlefield competition, with three receiving prizes and one gaining a place at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco. It gives selected founders exposure to investors and a route into a global startup showcase.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Offensive cybersecurity researchers told TechCrunch that safety guardrails built into AI systems from OpenAI and Anthropic can hinder work such as finding unknown vulnerabilities and developing exploit tools. Their complaint highlights a difficult boundary for AI providers: the same capabilities that can help legitimate security testing can also be used to attack systems. The debate may shape whether companies offer more controlled access for vetted researchers.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Mary Kate Golding, a 34-year-old set decorator whose credits included The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel, was found fatally stabbed in her Queens apartment on July 21, police said. Her husband, Joseph Azzaretto, was later found dead by hanging nearby, and authorities have described the deaths as a suspected murder-suicide; the couple’s 11-month-old son was unharmed. The NYPD investigation remains the key process for formally determining what happened.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The FDA is deciding whether seven peptides, including compounds such as BPC-157 and TB-500, can legally be made by compounding pharmacies in the United States. A favorable decision could make the substances more broadly available outside conventional FDA-approved drug channels, while an unfavorable one would restrict that route. The agency’s ruling will matter for patients and providers seeking access, as well as for oversight of products often marketed for recovery or performance.

stories.delivered_paragraph: An Indonesian court convicted 19 people in a baby-trafficking case involving at least 34 children, including at least 12 sent to Singapore for adoption. Both governments now face a sensitive decision balancing the children’s legal status, welfare and ties to the families caring for them.

stories.delivered_paragraph: ChangXin Memory Technologies, China’s largest memory-chip maker, raised $8.6 billion in Asia’s biggest IPO this year and is expected to begin trading on Shanghai’s STAR Market on July 27. Investors fear its valuation could quickly exceed 1 trillion yuan ($139 billion), forcing index and sector funds to shift money into the stock and draining liquidity from other Chinese technology shares. That repositioning has already pressured chip and domestic-substitution sectors that had led the market rally.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Japan’s core consumer inflation rose to 1.6% in June, its first increase since March, as higher oil costs spread through the economy. Headline inflation reached 1.7%, while the producer-price index jumped 7.1%, its highest level since March 2023, underscoring the cost pressure businesses face despite consumer energy subsidies. Higher import costs from energy prices and a weak yen could complicate efforts to keep inflation contained.
